description: Executions whose expiry time is exactly equal to either the start or the end bound of the window are included in the per-order groups.

c.request: For order executions with an expiry time (`expirespot`) between '2025-02-28 08:29:46.10496' and '2025-03-13 08:29:46.068533' (comparing the values as text), group them by order (`ordersmark`) and work out each order's average unfilled quantity (`remaincount`, ignoring missing values) and its number of executions. Then give me one row with the average of those per-order averages (ignoring missing ones) and the total of the per-order execution counts, without rounding. Executions whose expiry time is exactly equal to either the start or the end bound of the window are included in the per-order groups.
c.sql: SELECT AVG(per_order_avg) AS avg_of_order_avg_remaincount, SUM(execution_count) AS total_executions FROM (SELECT ordersmark, AVG(remaincount) AS per_order_avg, COUNT(*) AS execution_count FROM orderexecutions WHERE expirespot BETWEEN '2025-02-28 08:29:46.10496' AND '2025-03-13 08:29:46.068533' GROUP BY ordersmark) AS per_order;

b.request: Include executions where `expirespot` (compared as text) is greater than or equal to '2025-02-28 08:29:46.10496' and less than or equal to '2025-03-13 08:29:46.068533'; group them by `ordersmark`, take each group's average `remaincount` ignoring NULLs and its execution count, then return the average of those per-order averages (ignoring NULLs) and the sum of the per-order counts, unrounded.
b.sql: WITH per_order AS (SELECT ordersmark, AVG(remaincount) AS avg_remain, COUNT(*) AS exec_count FROM orderexecutions WHERE CAST(expirespot AS TEXT) >= '2025-02-28 08:29:46.10496' AND CAST(expirespot AS TEXT) <= '2025-03-13 08:29:46.068533' GROUP BY ordersmark) SELECT AVG(avg_remain) AS avg_of_order_avg_remaincount, SUM(exec_count) AS total_execution_count FROM per_order;
b.raw: Include executions where `expirespot` (compared as text) is greater than or equal to '2025-02-28 08:29:46.10496' and less than or equal to '2025-03-13 08:29:46.068533'; group them by `ordersmark`, take each group's average `remaincount` ignoring NULLs and its execution count, then return the average of those per-order averages (ignoring NULLs) and the sum of the per-order counts, unrounded.

d.request: For order executions whose `expirespot` text is greater than or equal to '2025-02-28 08:29:46.10496' and less than or equal to '2025-03-13 08:29:46.068533', group by `ordersmark`, compute each group's average non-null `remaincount` and its execution count, then return one row with the unrounded average of those per-order averages (ignoring nulls) and the sum of the per-order counts.
d.sql: SELECT AVG(g.avg_remain) AS avg_of_order_avgs, SUM(g.exec_count) AS total_execution_count FROM (SELECT ordersmark, AVG(remaincount) AS avg_remain, COUNT(*) AS exec_count FROM orderexecutions WHERE expirespot >= '2025-02-28 08:29:46.10496' AND expirespot <= '2025-03-13 08:29:46.068533' GROUP BY ordersmark) AS g;

a.request: Looking only at order executions whose expiry time (`expirespot`) falls between '2025-02-28 08:29:46.10496' and '2025-03-13 08:29:46.068533', with both endpoints included (comparing the values as text), group them by order (`ordersmark`) and, for each order, compute the average unfilled quantity (`remaincount`, ignoring missing values) and the number of executions. Then give me one row with the average of those per-order averages (ignoring missing ones) and the total of the per-order execution counts, without rounding.
a.sql: SELECT AVG(per_order.avg_remain) AS avg_of_avg_remain, SUM(per_order.exec_count) AS total_exec_count FROM (SELECT ordersmark, AVG(remaincount) AS avg_remain, COUNT(*) AS exec_count FROM orderexecutions WHERE expirespot >= '2025-02-28 08:29:46.10496' AND expirespot <= '2025-03-13 08:29:46.068533' GROUP BY ordersmark) AS per_order;
